newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen down, extends Thursday loss.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen down, extends Thursday loss.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open lower Friday, extending Thursday's loss on bearish fundamentals and as part of a gradual retrenchment from strong gains made in June, market sources said.

In over-the-counter business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were talked at $32,00-32,50 a megawatt hour (MWh) down from Thursday's settlement at $33.10 and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at $22.00-22.50 against yesterday's close at $22.81.
If the complex continues to trend lower, analysts assessed chart support for August PV at $32.00 and August COB $21.50.

Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were forecast to be cooler-than-normal into early next week, while the Southwest was expected to see temperatures one to three degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the south and west and near normal elsewhere over the next several days.
In additional to seasonal weather, rising power supply in the West is expected to put downward pressure on the futures and Western cash power prices.

Electricity output at the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California was reduced to 90 percent of capacity early Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report.
The adjoining 1,080 MW unit 3 is expected to resume operation around July 10 after being taken offline April 12 for refueling.

The WNP-2 nuclear plant continued to await clearance from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission before beginning start-up operations, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday, adding the unit would be "physically ready" to resume operations by late tonight or early Friday.

Several Western coal-fired power units were also expected to return to the power grid over the next several days, including a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., a 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado.

Separately, the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council is expected to vote on a summer derating of the Pacific Intertie transmission system to 6,300 MW from the current 7,200 MW, beginning in early July.
